title: 1970 AHSME Problem 23
statement: The number \(10!\) (\(10\) is written in base \(10\)), when written in the base \(12\) system, ends in exactly \(k\) zeros. The value of \(k\) is:

solutions.text:
The prime exponents in \(10!\) are \[ \begin{gathered} v_2(10!)=5+2+1=8,\\ v_3(10!)=3+1=4. \end{gathered} \] Each factor of \(12=2^2\cdot3\) uses two factors of \(2\) and one of \(3.\) Hence the number of trailing base-\(12\) zeros is \[ \min\left(\left\lfloor\frac82\right\rfloor,4\right)=4. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: A trailing base-\(12\) zero contributes one factor of \(12=2^2\cdot3\)
Compare the exponents of \(2\) and \(3\) in \(10!\)
